criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001a: Identifies 24-month lookback deviation in service standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies the draft's 24-month service-standard lookback as a deviation and replaces it with a 12-month lookback. Both the redline comment C-01 and review memo C1 cite the APA/playbook basis and propose the required change.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001b: Identifies 'or better than' qualifier in service standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the draft’s “equal to or better than” language as creating a ratcheting standard, deletes it, and replaces it with a “substantially consistent” historical-performance standard. The review memo likewise identifies “equal to or better than” as a deviation requiring removal.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001c: Identifies undefined 'industry best practices' benchmark
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the “industry best practices” overlay in Section 3.1 as an expansive standard exceeding the APA benchmark and deletes it, replacing it with a 12-month historical “substantially consistent” standard. The memo likewise identifies the language as a deviation and recommends no external benchmark.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001d: Proposes redline conforming service standard to playbook
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 3.1 includes corrective replacement language requiring each Service to be provided “in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and quality at which such Service was provided to or on behalf of the Business during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the Closing Date,” which conforms to the specified playbook standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002a: Identifies liability cap as 200% of total fees vs. APA's trailing 12-month cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies that draft Section 10.1 caps liability at 200% of total Service Charges paid, contrasts it with APA Section 7.12(d)'s rolling cap based on fees actually paid during the 12 months preceding the claim, and quantifies the resulting exposure difference.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002b: Quantifies liability cap exposure difference
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly quantifies the cap exposure: approximately $41.004 million under the draft versus $13.464 million under the APA trailing-12-month cap, yielding an approximately $27.540 million gap (about 3.05x). These calculations are shown in both the markup and review memorandum and are in the required ballpark.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002c: Redlines liability cap to conform to APA Section 7.12(d)
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.1 proposes corrective redline language capping aggregate liability at total TSA fees actually paid during the 12 months immediately preceding the date the applicable claim is first asserted, expressly aligning the cap with APA Section 7.12(d).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003a: Identifies non-mutual consequential damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly identifies that Section 10.2 is one-way: Polaris waives consequential-damages claims against Trident, while Trident does not reciprocally waive such claims against Polaris, leaving Polaris exposed. It also proposes a mutual waiver.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003b: Redlines to make consequential damages waiver mutual
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.2 replaces the one-way waiver with an express mutual waiver stating that each party waives claims against the other for consequential, incidental, special, punitive, exemplary, or indirect damages, consistent with the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004a: Identifies automatic renewal extending TSA beyond 18 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The output flags Section 5.2’s two automatic six-month renewals after the 18-month initial term as extending the TSA beyond the APA’s 18-month hard stop, and deletes automatic renewal. Although it does not expressly state “30 months,” the maximum extension is clearly identified from the quoted terms.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004b: Redlines to delete auto-renewal and impose hard 18-month stop
criteria_results.reasoning: The markup deletes the automatic-renewal mechanism, provides that the Agreement expires after the 18-month Initial Term, and requires any individual-Service extension to be documented in a mutually signed written amendment. It also caps extensions at six months and applies cost-plus-15% pricing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005a: Identifies 120-day termination notice exceeding APA's 90 days
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags Section 5.3's 120-day notice requirement as conflicting with APA Section 7.12(c), states that the APA requires 90 days, and revises the provision accordingly.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005b: Redlines termination notice to 90 days per APA
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 5.3 redlines the individual-service termination notice period from 120 days to 90 days and expressly identifies APA Section 7.12(c) as the basis for the correction.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006a: Identifies Key Personnel consent right overriding Polaris staffing discretion
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the Key Personnel consent right in Section 4.3 and Schedule H as problematic because it gives Trident approval over reassignment and replacement of named employees, conflicting with Polaris’s sole staffing discretion under the playbook. It deletes the consent requirement, preserves Polaris’s discretion, and reiterates the issue in the review memo.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006b: Proposes compromise on Key Personnel (notice + qualified replacement)
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 4.3 restores Polaris’s sole discretion over staffing and removes Trident’s consent right, while offering the required compromise: where practicable, Polaris must provide 15 Business Days’ advance notice of planned reassignments or replacements and use commercially reasonable efforts to provide a reasonably qualified replacement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007a: Identifies IT services 15% markup exceeding APA 10% cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the IT Services markup as 15% ($391,000/month) instead of the APA-compliant 10% ($374,000/month), cites APA Section 7.12(b), and corrects the fee schedule accordingly.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007b: Correctly computes IT fee difference
criteria_results.reasoning: The output correctly calculates the IT fee difference as $17,000 per month ($391,000 minus $374,000) and $306,000 over 18 months.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007c: Notes APA compliance risk even though overcharge benefits Polaris
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly acknowledges that the erroneous 15% IT markup benefits Polaris but still must be corrected for APA compliance and credibility. Comment C-31 states Polaris should not retain the favorable miscalculation because APA compliance and credibility are more important, and the memo likewise identifies it as a seller-benefiting error requiring correction to the APA-compliant 10% markup.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008a: Identifies audit frequency deviation (twice/year vs. once/12 months)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that draft Section 14.1 permits audits twice per calendar year, cites the playbook's once-per-12-month limit, and redlines the provision to allow no more than one audit in any 12-month period.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008b: Identifies audit cost allocation deviation (Seller's vs. Buyer's expense)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that draft Section 14.1 places audits at Polaris’s expense, cites the playbook deviation, and redlines the provision so audits are conducted at Service Recipient’s (Buyer’s) sole expense. The review memo likewise identifies “seller pays” as a problem and proposes “buyer expense.”

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008c: Identifies audit notice period deviation (10 vs. 30 business days)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that draft Section 14.1 permits audits on 10 Business Days' notice, cites Playbook §9.1, and redlines the notice period to at least 30 Business Days. The review memo also repeats the 10-day deviation and proposed 30-day requirement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009a: Identifies Ohio governing law vs. playbook's Pennsylvania law
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags draft Section 15.1 as using Ohio law, cites the Polaris Playbook, and proposes replacing it with Pennsylvania law. The review memo likewise identifies Ohio law as the problem and Pennsylvania law as the seller position.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009b: Identifies Cuyahoga County litigation vs. playbook's AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags §15.2's Cuyahoga County, Ohio litigation provision as a playbook deviation and replaces it with executive escalation, optional mediation, and confidential binding arbitration administered by the AAA under its Commercial Arbitration Rules in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The review memo repeats this issue and proposed change.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009c: Explains strategic importance of home-state law and arbitration for Polaris
criteria_results.reasoning: The output explains the strategic rationale: it notes that Ohio law and Cuyahoga County litigation give Trident a home-state advantage, while Pennsylvania aligns with Polaris’s headquarters, personnel, and counsel. It also identifies arbitration benefits, including confidentiality, avoiding public dockets and broad discovery, and using Pittsburgh as Polaris’s home forum.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010a: Identifies overbroad perpetual IP license grant
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags Section 7.1’s perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable license covering Polaris tools, methodologies, templates, software, processes, and know-how as a critical, board-level departure from the playbook. It identifies the risk of proprietary operational IP leakage and competitive harm, and replaces the grant with a strict no-license reservation requiring any post-TSA use to be separately negotiated.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010b: Redlines to delete IP license and confirm Polaris sole ownership
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 7.1 deletes the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license in full and replaces it with language confirming Polaris and its affiliates retain all right, title, and interest in Service Provider Materials. It expressly grants no license or other IP interest, while permitting only limited access and use necessary to receive services during the applicable TSA service period, ending upon expiration or termination.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011a: Identifies missing non-solicitation provision
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft lacks protection against Trident hiring TSA personnel, identifies the non-solicitation provision as absent, and adds Section 15.12 restricting Trident from soliciting, recruiting, hiring, or engaging Polaris personnel who provided services.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011b: Drafts non-solicitation provision with 12-month post-service tail
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 15.12 restricts Trident from soliciting, recruiting, hiring, or engaging Polaris service personnel during the Term and for 12 months thereafter without Polaris’s prior written consent. This satisfies the required consent protection and 12-month post-service tail.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012a: Identifies CGL insurance reduction ($2M vs. $5M playbook)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft requires only $2 million in Buyer CGL coverage, cites the playbook, and proposes increasing the requirement to $5 million per occurrence and aggregate.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012b: Identifies missing umbrella coverage requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft omits umbrella coverage and proposes adding at least $5 million of umbrella or excess liability insurance in revised Section 13.1. The review memo also identifies the omission and recommends “$5M CGL + $5M umbrella.”

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012c: Identifies missing additional insured endorsement
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft omits additional-insured protection and revises Section 13.1 to require Polaris and its Affiliates to be named as additional insureds under the Buyer's CGL and umbrella/excess policies, with delivery of applicable endorsements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013a: Flags missing IMMEX program provisions for Monterrey facility
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the missing IMMEX provisions for the Monterrey facility and adds Schedule E, Section 6A allocating post-Closing responsibility to Trident for obtaining, maintaining, renewing, and complying with its IMMEX certification, while defining Polaris's transition assistance, notice duties, costs, and limitations. The review memo also identifies the omission as a critical issue.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013b: Flags missing Mexican data privacy (LFPDPPP) provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft covers only U.S. privacy law despite processing Mexican employees’ HR and payroll data, identifies the LFPDPPP by name, and adds substantive provisions addressing controller/processor roles, privacy notices, required consents and cross-border transfer authorizations, safeguards, incident notification, data-subject requests, return/deletion, and a supplemental data-processing addendum. The review memo also identifies this as a critical issue requiring Mexico/LatAm counsel confirmation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014a: Identifies missing termination assistance/wind-down provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft is silent on termination assistance/wind-down support and adds Section 5.5(e) providing up to 60 days of defined, compensated termination assistance. The review memo likewise identifies the absence and cites the Polaris Playbook §3.4.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014b: Proposes termination assistance at cost-plus-15% for up to 60 days
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent inserted Section 5.5(e), requiring reasonable termination assistance for a period not exceeding 60 days and pricing it at Service Provider's Fully-Loaded Cost plus 15%. This satisfies both required elements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015a: Identifies missing change order procedure
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the absence of a change-order mechanism in both the markup and review memo, noting that there is no formal process for additional services, material volume increases, or scope changes. It also adds a written, signed change-order procedure in Section 6.7, consistent with the playbook requirement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015b: Proposes change order procedure with cost-plus-15% pricing
criteria_results.reasoning: Proposed Section 6.7 requires a written change order signed by authorized representatives of both parties for additional services, material volume increases, or material scope changes, and specifies cost-plus-15% pricing unless otherwise agreed in writing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016a: Identifies vague payment terms ('commercially reasonable time')
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags “commercially reasonable time” in Section 6.3 as vague and replaces it with a defined payment period of 30 days after the invoice date. The review memo also identifies the issue and recommends Net 30, with Net 45 as a fallback.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016b: Redlines payment terms to Net 30 days
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 6.3 replaces the vague “commercially reasonable time” standard with payment of each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days after the invoice date, expressly implementing Net 30 terms.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016c: Adds late payment interest at 1.5%/month or max legal rate
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 6.3 adds that late amounts accrue interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, exactly satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017a: Identifies missing force majeure 90-day termination trigger
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft force majeure clause lacks a termination trigger and adds a provision allowing either party to terminate the affected service without penalty after a force majeure event continues for 90 consecutive days. The review memo also identifies this gap and cites the playbook.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017b: Proposes 90-day force majeure termination right
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 12.1 proposes that if a Force Majeure Event continues for 90 consecutive days and materially prevents performance, either party may terminate the affected service by written notice without penalty.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo produced as a deliverable
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent produced a seller-side TSA review memorandum that summarizes the key issues, priorities, quantified exposure, negotiation strategy, and related markup deliverable. This satisfies the requirement to produce a cover memorandum summarizing the TSA review.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo organizes issues by priority tiers (Critical/Significant/Minor)
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memo clearly organizes issues into three expressly labeled priority tiers: Tier 1 — Critical, Tier 2 — Significant, and Tier 3 — Minor / cleanup.

criteria_results.title: APA-conflict issues classified as highest priority in cover memo
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memo places all specified direct APA conflicts in Priority Tier 1—Critical: automatic renewal (C2), 120-day termination notice (C3), IT markup above 10% (C4), and the 200% liability cap (C5). It separately places pure playbook deviations in Priority Tier 2—Significant, clearly distinguishing their priority.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo includes negotiation strategy distinguishing firm vs. flexible positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo clearly distinguishes firm and flexible positions for well over three key issues and explains the basis. For example, the APA-mandated service standard, renewal, liability cap, indemnity, cross-border, and precedence provisions are labeled “Must change” or “Non-negotiable,” while significant playbook items include express fallbacks such as 90 days/cost-plus-10% for termination assistance, Net 45/1.0% for payment terms, and 120 days for force majeure. The negotiation sequence also directs the seller to preserve structural protections and trade only on identified timing, notice, or pricing details.

criteria_results.title: Redline markup includes proposed edits to the TSA
criteria_results.reasoning: The output provides a full marked-up TSA with numerous explicit deletions, additions, and substituted provisions throughout the agreement and schedules, rather than merely listing issues.

criteria_results.title: Redline markup includes explanatory comments for changes
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline includes numerous annotated comments (e.g., C-01 through C-31) explaining the basis, Polaris risk, and negotiation position for proposed changes, with references to APA provisions, the TSA Playbook, and client instructions. This satisfies the requirement for explanatory comments accompanying the edits.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies Polaris as Service Provider / Seller throughout
criteria_results.reasoning: The output consistently identifies Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. as the Seller and Service Provider and Trident as the Buyer and Service Recipient. The markup, comments, and review memorandum are framed throughout from Polaris’s perspective, emphasizing service-provider protections such as limiting liability, preserving IP and staffing discretion, controlling scope and renewals, and ensuring payment and audit protections.

criteria_results.title: References APA Section 7.12 when flagging APA-conflict issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent repeatedly cites APA Section 7.12 and relevant subsections when flagging APA conflicts, including §7.12(a) for term/renewal, §7.12(c) for the termination notice period, §7.12(b) for fee methodology and markup, and §7.12(d) for the liability cap and consequential-damages provisions.

criteria_results.title: Fee escalation provision addressed (playbook: greater of 3% or CPI-U)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly addresses fee escalation in Section 6.4, proposing annual adjustment by the greater of 3% or the CPI-U increase, and cites Playbook §4.2. The review memo also identifies this mechanism as the seller position.

criteria_results.title: Indemnification provision addressed (Buyer indemnifies for third-party claims)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly addresses indemnification in Sections 9.1–9.3 and the review memo. It revises Buyer’s indemnity to cover third-party claims arising from Buyer’s use of or reliance on the Services, subject to an exception for claims resulting from Seller’s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct, consistent with the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Both deliverable files are produced
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes two clearly distinct deliverables: (1) a marked-up/redlined TSA identified as “tsa-markup-redline.docx” and (2) a separate partner cover memorandum identified as “tsa-review-memo.docx.”

criteria_results.title: Correct total monthly service cost baseline ($1,020,000) referenced
criteria_results.reasoning: The output correctly references the $1,020,000 total monthly base cost in Schedule G and repeatedly identifies the corrected total monthly fee at a uniform 10% markup as $1,122,000, including in the review memo's fee calculations.

criteria_results.title: Playbook's dispute escalation to senior executives referenced
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 15.2 expressly requires disputes to be escalated first to the parties’ CFO- or General Counsel-level representatives for a 15-business-day resolution period before mediation or binding arbitration. The review memo also references executive escalation before AAA arbitration.

criteria_results.title: Redline comments explain specific risk to Polaris for at least five changes
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline includes well over five comments identifying concrete adverse consequences to Polaris. Examples include over-resourcing and prioritization burdens from the service standard (C-01), loss of staffing flexibility and employment-law complications (C-02), open-ended service obligations from automatic renewal (C-03), IP leakage and competitive harm from the perpetual license (C-11), Mexico privacy enforcement and employee-claim exposure (C-13/C-14), materially increased and quantified liability exposure under the 200% cap (C-17), and operational/customs penalties from omitted IMMEX allocation (C-29). These comments go beyond mechanical APA or playbook references and expressly explain Polaris-specific risks.
